text:
nina: quick heads-up — onboarding for `opus-1x-lite` failed in the HF->Redwood converter during tokenization step. converter log: FileNotFoundError for tokenizer.json even though tokenizer_config.json is present.

sam: can you paste the converter log and the model package tree?

nina: log snippet:
```
2026-03-19T14:02:11Z INFO converter: starting conversion for opus-1x-lite
2026-03-19T14:02:12Z ERROR converter.token: fast tokenizer load failed
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/converter/token_loader.py", line 78, in load_fast_tokenizer
    with open(os.path.join(path, 'tokenizer.json')) as f:
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/models/opus-1x-lite/tokenizer.json'

During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
  File "/app/converter/token_loader.py", line 110, in load_tokenizer
    raise TokenizationError('no usable tokenizer artifacts')
TokenizationError: no usable tokenizer artifacts
```

Model package listing (inside tar):
```
model.bin
config.json
tokenizer_config.json  # present
vocab.txt              # present for slow tokenizer
merges.txt             # present for bpe
```

sam: hmm, so slow tokenizer artifacts exist (vocab/merges) and tokenizer_config.json exists, but tokenizer.json (fast format) is missing. converter currently treats missing tokenizer.json as fatal because it prefers fast path.

jonathan: this smells like a packaging ordering/sideload race we saw before — the model builder writes tokenizer_config.json early, then parallel postprocessing writes tokenizer.json later, and converter picks up the package mid-flight when only one half exists. we used to see similar on windows snapshots.

nina: interesting — the package was created by the model-import job that runs parallel asset generation. job logs show two steps finishing ~1s apart. could be timing.

maya: short term workaround: synthesize a minimal tokenizer.json from tokenizer_config.json + vocab/merges during convert if tokenizer.json missing. it's imperfect but gets the fast loader to a safe fallback. snippet I used before: 
```python
# synth_tokenjson.py (very small shim)
import json, os
p = '/models/opus-1x-lite'
if not os.path.exists(os.path.join(p,'tokenizer.json')):
    cfg = json.load(open(os.path.join(p,'tokenizer_config.json')))
    tokenjson = {
        'version': cfg.get('model_max_length', 2),
        'model_spec': cfg.get('tokenizer_class', 'BPE'),
        'tokens': {},
    }
    # best-effort map special tokens
    for k in ['bos_token','eos_token','unk_token','pad_token','sep_token','cls_token']:
        if k in cfg:
            tokenjson.setdefault('special_tokens', {})[k] = cfg[k]
    json.dump(tokenjson, open(os.path.join(p,'tokenizer.json'),'w'))
    print('synthesized tokenizer.json')
```

jonathan: that could work as a short-term patch, but long-term we should avoid a hard failure: converter should accept slow-tokenizer artifacts if tokenizer.json missing, or attempt synthesis automatically. also add a package-atomicity check in the importer so we don't pick up half-baked tarballs.

sam: agreed. suggested approach: (1) quick hotfix in converter: try slow tokenizer path if tokenizer.json missing; (2) add atomic marker file `.package_complete` at end of packaging; importer ignores packages without it. (3) follow-up: converter synthesizes tokenjson with better mapping (use merges/vocab to populate).

maya: will open PRs for (1) and (2). PRs will include minimal unit tests: missing tokenizer.json -> converter falls back to slow loader and logs warning with link to onboarding guide. :eyes:

deploy-bot: PR maya/fix-tokenizer-fallback (#3287) merged to staging — will run e2e onboarding tests. :rocket:

nina: thanks — for the immediate stuck models in the queue I ran the synth_tokenjson.sh on 3 packages and they finished onboarding. leaving notes in the model-import ticket. :thumbsup:

sam: adding a small monitoring alert for TokenizationError spikes during onboarding so we catch regressions.

jonathan: long-term, we should also update our HF->Redwood conversion docs: document expected artifacts (tokenizer.json vs tokenizer_config.json, vocab/merges) and recommended packaging order. I'll draft a short checklist.

nina: perfect. filing follow-ups: M-3421 (atomic packaging), M-3422 (converter fallback), DOC-122 (docs).
